parts.text:
You read part of an interview. An analyst asked one future user of a software service a series of questions. You decide, for each question, whether it follows up the answer given just before it.

A question follows up the previous answer when it asks about something that answer said: it asks the speaker to explain, give an example of, say more about, or say why of something the answer mentioned, or it picks up a particular thing the answer named. Wording does not matter; a question can follow up an answer without repeating any of its words.

A question does not follow up the previous answer when it turns to something that answer did not mention, even if the speaker said it in an earlier answer, even if it stays with the same broad subject, and even if it is a good question. A general question that could follow any answer, such as whether there is anything else, does not follow up either.

You receive the pairs of the interview after its first question: for each later question, the answer given just before it, and the question.

Reply with JSON only: an object with one key, "questions", a list with exactly one entry for every pair, in the same order. Each entry has "id", the question's id, and "follow_up", true or false.

Q2
The answer just before it: Each company has its own pads at its own sites. A pad is never lent to another company.
The question: So what happens when all of your pads at one site are taken?

Q3
The answer just before it: The drone waits, or it flies to another of our sites if it has the battery.
The question: Earlier you said pads are never lent. Has anyone ever asked to borrow one?

Q4
The answer just before it: Not that I know of.
The question: How do drones report where they are?

Q5
The answer just before it: Through relay stations. When coverage is patchy their reports come late, out of order, or twice.
The question: What does it mean for you when a report comes twice?

Q6
The answer just before it: Nothing, as long as nobody counts it twice. It is the late ones that confuse people.
The question: Confuse them how?

Q7
The answer just before it: A late report can say a drone is back over a field when it already landed.
The question: Are there other ways the reports mislead you?

Q8
The answer just before it: When a drone restarts in the air it starts counting its reports again from the beginning.
The question: Let us talk about sensors. Which sensors do your drones carry?

Q9
The answer just before it: Cameras, thermal cameras and laser scanners, and the models differ.
The question: Does it matter to you which model has which sensor?

Q10
The answer just before it: For inspections it does. An inspection needs the right sensor on board.
The question: What is the most important thing a new service must never do?

Q11
The answer just before it: Mix up our drones with another company's.
The question: Has that ever happened?
